name: Lip competence training

lead: Lip competence training means keeping the lips gently sealed at rest, a habit oral-posture communities practice for better jaw and facial development and a more closed, composed look.

In orthodontics, lip competence is a clinical descriptor meaning the lips close at rest without strain. A sealed-lip position is also a core element of mewing, alongside tongue posture, lightly touching teeth and nasal breathing. No reviewed study tests whether training lip closure changes facial structure.

paras: Practitioners close the lips softly, breathe through the nose and hold the position through the day as part of a routine with tongue posture. Some use mouth taping at night to encourage closure.
Reference sources say mouth taping used to encourage lip closure carries risks and needs professional supervision.

angle.text: Oral-posture communities practice resting with sealed lips, saying it guides jaw growth and supports facial development. It is done as an everyday habit alongside nasal breathing and tongue posture. Lip competence is an orthodontic descriptor, and no study tests training it.

lead: Lip competence training is the habit of keeping the lips gently sealed at rest, treated in some oral-posture communities as a posture skill that is said to support jaw and facial development. In orthodontics, lip competence is a clinical descriptor meaning the lips can close at rest without strain, and lip incompetence means they cannot.[1]

A sealed-lip position is also listed as a core element of mewing, alongside tongue posture, lightly touching teeth and nasal breathing.[2] No reviewed study tests whether training lip closure changes facial structure.
infobox: Not directly studied in sources reviewed

paras: Practice guidance in mewing descriptions is to close the lips softly while breathing through the nose.[2] Some practitioners use mouth taping to encourage lip closure during sleep, which a reference article says carries risks and needs professional supervision.[2]

In dentistry and oral surgery, lip competence is a recorded feature of the face. A 1977 report on surgical-orthodontic correction of skeletal open bite lists lip incompetence among indications for the procedure and lip competence among contraindications for a particular type of case.[1] Orthodontic studies also record lip coverage as a variable, for example in a population study of incisor trauma in adolescents that tested for effects of lip coverage among other factors.[3]

No studies found that test lip competence training as an intervention for facial appearance. Clinical literature records lip competence as a feature associated with bite type and dental trauma risk, but that work does not evaluate a training programme.[1][3] 2025 pilot studies of orofacial myofunctional therapy reported effects on hyoid position and jaw pain but did not directly test mewing or lip sealing.[2]

lore.intro: Lip seal is discussed alongside tongue posture and nasal breathing as part of an overall posture routine.

claims.claim: Keeping the lips sealed at rest improves jaw and facial development.
